issue_title: Reject duplicate widget names within a tenant
issue_body:
Two widgets of the same tenant can currently share a name, which breaks the name-based lookups support uses.

`POST /widgets` with a name another widget of the same tenant already has must return `409 Conflict` with error code `duplicate_name`. Names are compared case-insensitively. Different tenants may reuse a name. An empty name keeps returning `400` with error code `invalid_name`.

plan.summary: Enforce per-tenant unique widget names with a unique index and a duplicate_name API error.

approach.description: Add migration 0015 creating a unique index on widgets (tenant_id, lower(name)), with a down migration dropping it.
In CreateWidget, detect the unique violation (pgcode 23505) and return store.ErrDuplicateName.
In the POST /widgets handler, map store.ErrDuplicateName to an API error with code duplicate_name and HTTP 400, matching the validation errors.
Keep the existing empty-name check returning 400 with code invalid_name.

verification.test_strategy: Store test: a second CreateWidget with the same tenant and a differently-cased name returns ErrDuplicateName. Handler tests: the duplicate, cross-tenant and empty-name cases each assert the status code and the error code.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR and run the 0015 down migration to drop the index.

acceptance_criteria.statement: POST /widgets with a name no other widget of the tenant uses returns HTTP 201.
POST /widgets with a name another widget of the same tenant already uses returns HTTP 400 with error code duplicate_name.
POST /widgets with the name "Gizmo" when the tenant has a widget named "gizmo" is refused like any duplicate.
POST /widgets with a name only another tenant uses returns HTTP 201.
POST /widgets with an empty name returns HTTP 400 with error code invalid_name.

risks_and_assumptions: No tenant holds duplicate names today; the index creation fails otherwise and must be preceded by a data fix.

catching_examples.note: ac-create-duplicate-400 contradicts the issue: a duplicate name must return 409 Conflict, not 400.
ac-create-duplicate-400 expects HTTP 400, but the issue specifies 409 for a duplicate name; approach step 3 maps the wrong code too.
The criterion for a name another widget already uses expects 400 with duplicate_name, which is at odds with the issue's 409 Conflict.

non_catching_examples.note: No test covers two concurrent creates racing on the same name; the unique index decides, so assert the loser's response.
Building the unique index on a large widgets table locks writes; create it concurrently.
Document the duplicate_name error code in api/openapi.yaml.
ac-create-duplicate-400 should also assert the response body carries the existing widget's id.
Renaming a widget via PATCH /widgets/{id} can also produce a duplicate; the plan changes only POST.
